battle.name: 漢平滇國之戰
battle.theater: 滇池東岸晉寧石寨山一帶
battle.brief: 公元前109年（漢武帝元初元年），漢廷以打通西南夷道為由，發蜀郡、犍為、益州郡兵南下滇池，迫滇國臣服，平後置益州郡，郡治滇池縣，並賜滇王金印。卡面的斯巴達長矛屬前800年前後的希臘方陣兵器，與本役相隔近七百年，不在此役現場；滇軍用銅戈、銅矛與弩，漢軍用鐵矛、環首刀與蹶張弩。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭是西漢中央對滇池王國的一次用兵，發生在漢武帝元初元年（公元前109年），主戰場在今雲南昆明晉寧一帶的滇池沿岸。漢朝一方是以郡兵為骨幹的中央直轄部隊：自成都南下的蜀郡、犍為郡及新置西南各郡的徵發兵員，步卒為主，配屬弩手、弓手與少量騎兵，由中樞派出的武官率領，前線屯駐在通往滇池的僰道與牂柯江一線；漢廷的戰略意圖很直接——在蜀郡之南、在夜郎與南越之間插入一個由漢朝掌控的郡，把西南夷道的一頭釘在滇池。滇國一方則是以滇王為最高統治者、以「君長」為地方首領的青銅王國：滇王居滇池之旁，控制石寨山、官渡一帶的王墓區與大片池畔耕地，並以貢賦方式統轄昆明、哀牢、越巂等部族，兵制以滇王直屬的武裝集團為骨幹，銅戈、銅矛、銅劍與弩、弓為主體，軍隊多在池畔與山間就地表達。所謂第三方，多數並非中立國，而是同一條西南通道上的各段主人：夜郎在今貴州一帶已於前111年置郡，越巂、沈犁、徙郡同時立郡，昆明與哀牢諸部則仍在漢朝邊緣，既與滇國往來，也各自求漢廷保護。漢、滇之間因此不是兩國相爭，而是同一條路上兩種秩序的碰撞：一方要把道路收歸郡縣，一方要在自己的池邊把貢賦與兵源管到底。
countriesEn: This war was a campaign by the Western Han court against the kingdom of Dian in the Dianchi basin, fought in the first year of Yuanchu (109 BC) under Emperor Wu of Han, with the main theatre on the shores of Dianchi around present-day Jinning in Kunming, Yunnan. The Han side was a centrally directed force built on the militia of the commanderies: men levied from Shu Commandery, from Qianwei and from the newly established commanderies of the south-west, infantry for the most part, with crossbowmen, archers and a small number of horsemen, led by officers appointed from the capital, with the forward echelon stationed along the Bin road and the Zhangke River that led to the lake. The strategic intent of the court was plain — to plant a Han-controlled commandery south of Shu, between the lands of Yelang and of Nanyue, and to nail the western end of the south-western road down at Dianchi. The Dian side was a bronze-age kingdom ruled by the king of Dian at its head, with local chiefs below him: the king sat beside the lake, controlled the royal cemetery area at Shizhaishan and at Guandu and a wide stretch of fields along the shore, and drew tribute from the peoples of Kunming, of Ailao and of Yuexi, its armed strength resting on the standing war-band of the royal house, armed mainly with bronze gous, bronze maos, bronze swords, crossbows and bows, and fighting for the most part on the ground of the lake shore and of the hills. The supposed third parties were for the most part not neutral states but the separate masters of one and the same road: Yelang, in what is now Guizhou, had already been made a commandery in 111 BC, and Yuexi, Shenli and Xiyi were established in the same year, while the peoples of Kunming and of Ailao remained on the Han frontier, dealing with Dian on the one hand and seeking Han protection on the other. The encounter between Han and Dian was therefore not a war between two states but a collision between two orders on one road: one side meant to bring the road under commandery and county administration, the other determined to keep the tribute and the flow of spears out of its own ponds.
people: 決策者是漢武帝劉徹。漢朝經營西南並非出於一時之興，而是從建元六年（前135年）遣唐蒙通夜郎起，一步步鋪開：博望侯張騫在元狩年間言西南夷可通身毒，漢廷先後派使十餘輩西行探路，卻屢屢受阻於滇池一帶的昆明諸部；張騫所議築的昆明池於前120年落成於長安西南，操演水軍與騎射，成為漢朝預想西南與西域的實驗場。滇國那邊，記錄中沒有留下名字的滇王與各部首領，是把漢使從滇池前趕走的關鍵人物；史書記滇國君長與漢使者相問「漢孰與我大」，語氣裡並無臣服之意。前109年出兵時，漢廷的實際統率者被記在使者與將吏一列的「武將」名下，正史未留其名，因此只能從部署反推其作為：分兵、分道、水陸並進，而不是單路直趨。決定性的物證不在史書而在地下：1956年，昆明晉寧石寨山古墓群出土一枚漢代金印「滇王之印」，方形，約2.4厘米見方，鈕作蟠螭形，印文四字篆書；這枚印說明漢廷在滇國覆亡之後仍保留了「滇王」的名號，把它授給滇國王室的一支，使其在益州郡的體系裡保留祭祀與統屬的名分。記滇國覆亡的《史記·西南夷列傳》與《漢書·西南夷傳》，正是司馬遷與班固根據漢廷檔案與使者回報編成的，所以戰後對滇的記載多從郡縣建置說起。
peopleEn: The decision-maker was Emperor Wu of Han, Liu Che. Han policy in the south-west was not a sudden mood but something built up step by step from the sending of Tang Meng to Yelang in the sixth year of Jianyuan (135 BC): the Marquis of Bowang, Zhang Qian, reported during the Yuanshou years that the south-western peoples offered a road to Shendu, the court sent a dozen or more envoys westward to find it, and again and again they were blocked by the peoples of Kunming around the lake; the Kunming Pool that Zhang Qian had argued for was completed in 120 BC to the south-west of the capital at Chang'an, where the fleet and the mounted archery were trained, and the capital became an experimental station for Han ideas about the south-west and the western regions. On the Dian side, the king of Dian and the local chiefs, whose names the records do not preserve, were the people who turned the Han envoys back from the lake; the histories record the ruler of Dian putting the question to a Han envoy, 'Han — how do you compare with us?', a question that carried no sense of submission. When the troops moved out in 109 BC, the actual commander on the Han side is listed only among envoys and officers as an unnamed 'military commander', and the only way to reconstruct his conduct is from the deployment: divided columns, divided roads, advance by land and by water together, rather than a single thrust. The decisive evidence is not in the histories but in the ground: in 1956 a Han gold seal was unearthed from the ancient cemetery at Shizhaishan in Jinning, Kunming, square, about 2.4 cm across, with a knob in the form of intertwined dragons and four characters in seal script reading 'Seal of the King of Dian'. This seal shows that after the fall of Dian the court kept the title 'king of Dian' alive, conferring it on one branch of the royal house so that it might retain, inside the commandery system, the duties of sacrifice and of nominal allegiance. The histories that record the end of Dian, the liezhuan on the south-western peoples in the Shiji and the account of the south-western peoples in the Hanshu, were composed by Sima Qian and Ban Gu from the court's own records and the reports of envoys, which is why what they say about Dian after the fighting is largely framed in terms of the setting up of commanderies.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛是希臘方陣的長兵器：兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套，方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。它成型於斯巴達與重裝步兵方陣盛行的年代（約公元前800年前後），到公元前109年已過去近七百載，滇池岸邊不可能出現這種武器，本場戰役真正交手的兵器完全是另一套東西。滇國的兵器以青銅為主：青銅戈的援部寬弧而內折，多不設胡，與戰國中原的三角援戈形制不同；青銅矛中脊隆起、通體飾菱形格紋；最具辨識度的是被稱為「祭祀長刀」的青銅直刃器，格首常飾人頭、虎頭或立人形象，與中原青銅劍判然有別；此外還有銅斧、銅錞與成組的銅戈，用以象徵武權。滇國的防護以皮甲、木盾為主，金屬甲胄極少，銅料主要流向貯貝器、銅鼓與禮器，這是青銅時代西南王國的典型結構。滇人善弩，銅弩機零件在滇文化遺址中出土。漢軍那邊則是鐵器與弩機的天下：環首刀、鐵矛鐵戟、劍、大盾，配蹶張弩與弓的階梯射擊，護具以札甲與皮甲為主，後勤靠牛車、騾馬馱載糧秣。兩軍都沒有希臘式的密集槍陣，但都在各自的池塘與山口之間，靠手裡的長兵與弩，決定誰能站到最後。
kitsEn: The card's dory is the long weapon of the Greek phalanx: a wooden shaft two metres long with a bronze ferrule at the butt, in the phalanx it decided who would still be standing long before the sword did. It was a form belonging to the age of Sparta and of the heavy infantry phalanx, roughly 800 BC, and by 109 BC nearly seven centuries had passed, so such a weapon could not have appeared on the shore of Dianchi; the arms that actually met in this campaign belonged to an entirely different order. The weapons of Dian were bronze: bronze gous with a broad curving blade folding inward and in most cases no hu, quite unlike the triangular-bladed gous of the Warring States in the central plains; bronze maos with a prominent midrib and lozenge-pattern decoration over the whole surface; most distinctive of all the bronze straight-edged blades known as 'ritual sabres', whose hilts are commonly decorated with a human head, a tiger's head or a standing figure, a form clearly distinct from the bronze swords of the central plains; besides these, bronze axes, bronze bells and sets of bronze gous, all of them tokens of military authority. Protection in Dian was by leather armour and wooden shields, metal body armour was extremely scarce, and the bronze went mostly into cowrie containers, into bronze drums and into ritual vessels — the typical structure of a south-western bronze-age kingdom. The Dian were at home with the crossbow, and bronze crossbow trigger parts have been recovered from Dian sites. On the Han side the world of iron and of the crossbow prevailed: ring-pommel sabres, iron spears and halberds, swords and large shields, with the tiered shooting of the crossbow and the bow, body protection of lamellar and of leather armour, and the baggage carried on ox carts and on mules and horses. Neither army had the dense spear phalanx of Greece, but each of them decided, between its own pond and its own mountain gaps, with the polearms and the crossbows in its hands, who would be left standing at the end.
tactics: 漢軍的打法是典型的邊疆長距離攻勢：第一步是「諭」——先遣使往滇池，陳說利害，漢朝在西南此前每一次開兵都以此為前奏，失敗才動手；第二步是分道進軍，兵分數路自成都沿僰道南下，一路由牂柯江方向切入，一路由滇池東岸的高地逼近，兩路約期合擊，企圖以多面進逼代替正面強攻；第三步是對壘——漢軍在滇池周邊的池岸平地與山間通道列陣，前排大盾與長兵成列，弩手在後列覆蓋射擊，以弩的壓制換取接近的距離，這是漢軍在南方叢林與丘陵地形中最倚重的手段；滇國軍則充分利用滇池的岸線與螺螄山、馬鞍山一帶的居高位置，以弓弩在林莽與山道間狙擊漢軍的側翼與糧隊，逼迫漢軍分兵護糧，而不是全力攻堅。第四步是切斷與圍困：漢軍占領節制通往哀牢、昆明諸部的山口，斷其外援與貢賦往來，再逼近滇池。滇國的最後選擇是退守城壘、遣使求援於鄰部，但漢朝既已把郡兵壓到池邊，任何等待都意味著消耗。滇人熟悉的銅戈與弩在守壘中仍有價值，但銅兵器的鈍重在長期圍攻的消耗裡終究抵不過鐵兵；滇國的崩解因此不是被一次衝鋒摧垮，而是在一次次斷糧、斷援與歸順中被逐步抽走。
tacticsEn: The Han method was that of a long-range offensive on a frontier. The first step was to admonish: to send envoys ahead to the lake and set out the rights and wrongs of the case, a formula the Han had followed before every war in the south-west, and only after that came the troops. The second step was advance by several roads, the force splitting into columns that came south from Chengdu along the Bin road, one cutting in by way of the Zhangke River and another closing in along the high ground east of the lake, the two timed to strike together, an attempt to bring pressure from several sides instead of hurling the whole army at a single front. The third step was the meeting of the lines: the Han formed up on the flats along the shore of the lake and in the mountain passes, large shields and polearms in front, crossbowmen behind them covering the ground with volleys, buying with the crossbow the distance needed to close, which was the weapon the Han relied on most in the wooded and hilly country of the south. The Dian in turn used the shoreline of the lake and the heights of Luosishan and of Ma'anshan to their advantage, shooting with bows and crossbows from the trees and the mountain tracks at the flanks and at the baggage trains of the Han, forcing the Han to split forces to guard the supplies rather than to attack with everything at once. The fourth step was cut and encirclement: the Han seized the passes that commanded the routes to Ailao and to the peoples of Kunming, cutting off Dian's outside help and its tribute traffic, and then closed in on the lake. Dian's last option was to fall back behind the fortifications and to send envoys to the neighbouring peoples for help, but with Han commandery troops already at the water's edge any delay meant only consumption. The bronze gous and crossbows the Dian knew well still had their value in the defence of a fort, but in the long attrition of a siege the weight of bronze could not hold against iron. Dian's collapse was therefore not the work of a single charge, but of being drawn out step by step by successive cuts of grain, of aid and of surrender.
data: 可考的數字大致如下。時間：公元前109年，漢武帝元初元年；此前一年（前111年）漢平南越，置南海、桂林、象郡，並同時立越巂郡、沈犁郡、徙郡，前120年（元狩三年）在長安西南築昆明池。距離：自成都沿僰道南下至滇池，行程約九百公里、近二千里，山道險仄，糧秣全賴人背牛馱。兵力：《史記》只說漢「發蜀郡、犍為、益州郡兵」，未載確切人數；以當時各郡可徵之卒推估，總量當在數萬量級，但這只是量級而非確數，正史的戰役記載在此確實空缺。月令：出兵月份在傳世史籍中沒有留下記載，卡面取九月，取的是漢廷於秋冬之際在西南用兵的一般部署，能確定的只有出兵在元初元年之內。滇國方面，能確認的是它的物質基礎：滇文化遺址以石寨山墓群為代表，1950年代先後發掘的墓葬編號至十三號，出土文物逾一萬件，其中貯貝器（盛貝幣的青銅器）數百件，銅鼓、銅戈、銅矛、銅劍、祭祀長刀與銅弩機零件成套出現；滇王之印出土於石寨山六號墓，金質，印面約2.4厘米見方，鈕作蟠螭形，印文「滇王之印」四字篆書，現藏雲南省博物館。石寨山墓葬一般分為四期，晚期約當西漢武帝至王莽之世，與滇國覆亡的年代銜接。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. Date: 109 BC, the first year of Yuanchu under Emperor Wu of Han; the year before (111 BC) the Han conquered Nanyue and founded the commanderies of Nanhai, of Guilin and of Xiang, and at the same time set up the commanderies of Yuexi, of Shenli and of Xiyi, and in 120 BC, the third year of Yuanshou, the Kunming Pool was dug to the south-west of the capital at Chang'an. Distance: from Chengdu southward along the Bin road to Dianchi is a march of about nine hundred kilometres, close to two thousand li, over steep tracks, with all grain and forage carried on men's backs and on pack animals. Strength: the Shiji says only that the Han 'levied the men of Shu, of Qianwei and of Yizhou', without giving a number; judging by what the commanderies of the time could furnish, the total must have been of the order of tens of thousands, but that is an order of magnitude and not a figure, and here the transmitted record of the battle is genuinely blank. Month: the month of departure is not preserved in the transmitted histories, and the card takes September, following the general pattern of Han campaigning in the south-west in the autumn and winter; all that can be fixed is that the operation fell within the first year of Yuanchu. On the Dian side what can be confirmed is its material base: the Dian culture is represented by the cemetery at Shizhaishan, where burials numbered up to thirteen were excavated in the 1950s, yielding more than ten thousand objects, among them several hundred cowrie containers (bronze vessels for cowrie currency), with bronze drums, bronze gous, bronze maos, bronze swords, ritual sabres and bronze crossbow trigger parts appearing in sets. The gold seal of the king of Dian came out of tomb number six at Shizhaishan: gold, about 2.4 cm square, with a knob in the form of intertwined dragons and four characters in seal script reading 'Seal of the King of Dian', now in the Yunnan Provincial Museum. The cemetery at Shizhaishan is generally divided into four phases, the latest corresponding roughly to the reign of Emperor Wu and to the time of Wang Mang, which fits the date of the fall of Dian.
cause: 這場戰爭的直接起因是道路。前111年漢朝平定南越、設置郡縣之後，從長安到南海的通道只剩一段斷口：雲南高原上的滇池地區仍由滇王與其屬部控制，漢使者往西南夷「十餘輩出此」，多數在昆明一帶被阻，「身毒道」因而無法打通。漢廷要的是從巴蜀經滇池、夜郎到交趾、番禺的連續路線——既有使節與商旅的通行，也有蜀郡對高原物資的取得，而更重要的是，把西南邊界畫成一條可以派兵防守的線。滇國的拒絕不僅是外交上的矜持，也是實力的自信：它有滇池的水、池畔的田與成片的牛羊，銅器製作與祭祀體系完整，其君長面對漢使時的反問「漢孰與我大」說明，它並不認為漢朝有力量讓自己低頭。於是漢廷把一條被封死的商路、一個不肯歸附的鄰邦，和「西南夷不可終日不制」的體面問題合在一起，最終決定用兵。前111年的南越已平，匈奴在元狩年間受挫於漠北，漢廷在西、南兩翼同時有餘力，這是元初元年能抽出兵力深入滇池的外部條件。
causeEn: The immediate cause of this war was a road. After the Han had conquered Nanyue and set up commanderies in 111 BC, only one gap remained in the line running from Chang'an to the South Sea: the region of Dianchi on the Yunnan plateau was still held by the king of Dian and his dependants, Han envoys going to the south-western peoples — a dozen or more going out this way — were repeatedly stopped in the Kunming area, and the road to Shendu could not be opened. What the court wanted was an unbroken route from Bashu through Dianchi, Yelang and Jiaozhi to Panyu: not only the passage of envoys and merchants and the acquisition of highland goods for Shu, but above all a border that could be drawn as a line along which troops could be posted. Dian's refusal was not merely diplomatic pride but confidence in its own strength: it had the water of the lake, the fields along the shore and the herds of cattle and sheep, and a complete system of bronze casting and of ritual, and when its ruler put the question to a Han envoy — Han, how do you compare with us? — it did not suppose that the Han had the power to make it bow. The court therefore joined together a blocked trade road, a neighbour that would not submit, and the question of face, that the south-western peoples could not be left ungoverned indefinitely, and decided on force. Nanyue had been settled in 111 BC and the Xiongnu had been checked in the northern steppe during the Yuanshou years, so the Han had strength to spare in the west and in the south at once; that was the external condition which allowed troops to be drawn out into the Dianchi basin in the first year of Yuanchu.
impact: 滇池平定之後，西南的歷史換了一條河道。益州郡的設立把滇池地區納入漢帝國的郡縣體系，滇國從獨立的青銅王國變為漢朝邊郡之內的封屬：滇王的封號與祭祀權被保留在郡縣體制之內，漢廷用一枚金印把這層關係固定下來——滇王之印如今是雲南考古最硬的一塊石頭之一。制度層面的影響更長遠：益州郡往後與越巂郡合為益州刺史部，漢王朝在南中設郡置吏、移民屯田的格局由此奠定；哀牢、昆明諸部先後被納入羈縻與內屬的體系，昆明池的水軍操練經驗與西南的水陸轉運一直沿用到東漢。物質面上，漢式鐵器、弩機、漆器與陶罐大量流入滇地，滇池周邊的牛耕與稻作在此後數百年逐步推開，雲南由青銅時代轉入鐵器時代的轉折點，學界多把它放在這個世紀的中段。文化上則是雙向的：滇的銅鼓與貯貝器造像隨著漢朝的收藏與祭祀進入中原，漢式行政、度量與文字也隨郡縣進入滇池；滇王之印後來在漢家手裡流轉，說明一件地方權力的象徵物被國家權力吸收，雲南自此進入中原王朝主導的歷史敘事。對漢朝本身，益州郡意味著西南邊界從「不確定」變成「可派兵」，代價則是山地後勤與地方治理的成本在往後幾百年裡一直存在。
impactEn: After Dianchi was settled, the history of the south-west changed its course. The establishment of Yizhou Commandery brought the lake region inside the commandery and county system of the Han empire, and Dian changed from an independent bronze-age kingdom into a feudatory within a Han border commandery: the title of king of Dian and the right of sacrifice were kept, but inside the commandery system, and the court fixed that relationship with one gold seal — the seal of the king of Dian, which today is one of the hardest stones of Yunnan archaeology. The institutional consequences ran much further: Yizhou Commandery was later joined with Yuexi to form the Yizhou Inspectorate, and the Han practice of posting officials, of colonising farms and of settling the south from there was set; the peoples of Ailao and of Kunming were drawn in turn into the system of jimi dependence and of inner affiliation, and the experience of fleet training at Kunming Pool and of water-and-land transport in the south-west was carried on into the Eastern Han. On the material side Han iron, crossbow triggers, lacquerware and pottery flowed in quantity into the Dian lands, and ox-ploughing and rice cultivation spread around the lake over the centuries that followed, so that Yunnan turned from the bronze age into the iron age, a transition that scholarship usually places around the middle of that century. The cultural movement ran both ways: the bronze drums and the cowrie containers of Dian entered the collections and the rituals of the central plains through the Han, while Han administration, weights and script entered Dianchi with the commandery; the seal of the king of Dian later passed through Han hands, which is to say that a token of local power was absorbed by state power, and from this point Yunnan entered the historical narrative led by the central plains. For the Han itself, Yizhou Commandery meant that the south-western frontier changed from uncertain to a place where troops can be posted, at the cost of mountain logistics and of the governance of the district, a cost that remained for the centuries to come.
result: 公元前109年這場戰爭的結局，是滇國作為獨立王國的終結與漢朝郡縣體系的落地。漢軍進至滇池，滇王失勢，其統治集團瓦解；漢廷沒有把滇國連根拔除，而是拆出其王室的一支另封為滇王，賜以「滇王之印」金印，令其在新置的益州郡內保留祭祀與名分之責，郡治設在滇池縣，漢朝的郡守、軍吏與滇王在同一套框架裡各司其職。戰役的技術性結果因此是雙份的：對漢朝，滇池與牂柯江、僰道連成一條可以常年通行的西南線，日後南中經營與南方絲路皆以此為樞紐；對滇國，銅戈、銅矛與祭祀長刀所代表的青銅王國的武裝傳統中斷，銅鼓的大型鑄造中心從滇池一帶南移，貴族階層隨王墓的封閉而消失，馬上在水塘邊用銅器行祭的秩序也隨之散去。真正的收尾還要更久：哀牢、昆明諸部在此後數十年陸續叛而復叛，漢朝先後以郡兵討伐與羈縻安置並用，直到東漢初年滇池地區的基本格局才真正穩定下來。可以確定的是，公元前109年之後，滇池不再是邊外之地，而是帝國的西南門戶；不能確定的是，這道門戶在未來兩千年裡究竟被守得有多好。
resultEn: The outcome of the campaign of 109 BC was the end of Dian as an independent kingdom and the grounding of the Han commandery system. The Han reached Dianchi, the king of Dian lost his position and his ruling group broke apart; the court did not erase Dian entirely, but cut out a branch of the royal house and enfeoffed it anew as king of Dian, granting it the gold seal reading 'Seal of the King of Dian' and assigning it the duties of sacrifice and of nominal standing within the newly established Yizhou Commandery, whose seat was placed at Dianchi county, so that the Han commandery officials and military clerks and the king of Dian now served out the same framework, each in his own office. The technical result of the war was therefore twofold: for the Han, Dianchi was joined with the Zhangke River and the Bin road into a south-western line passable the year round, which later became the pivot of Han operations in Nanzhong and of the southern silk road; for Dian, the armed tradition represented by the bronze gou, the bronze mao and the ritual sabre was broken off, the centre of large-scale bronze drum casting moved south away from the lake, the aristocratic class disappeared with the sealing of the royal tombs, and the order that had kept bronze vessels and horses by the water for ritual purposes fell apart with it. The real conclusion took longer still: the peoples of Ailao and of Kunming rebelled and were resubmitted over the following decades, and the court had to work with them through a mixture of commandery troops and jimi settlement, and it was not until the early Eastern Han that the basic pattern around Dianchi truly settled down. What can be certain is that after 109 BC the lake was no longer a place beyond the frontier but the empire's south-western gate; what cannot be certain is how well that gate was kept over the next two thousand years.
